decide_leak_HQ246_OPEN_001.author_claim: ~15 allocated blocks per decide() call, localized to the post-loop source-ref ordering block but not isolated further

independent_measurement.method: warm 3000 calls, gc.collect(), gc.disable(), sys.getallocatedblocks() delta per call; non-constant trusted hash so the request never enters the crashing positive path
independent_measurement.conclusion: the leak is exactly ~17.0 blocks per call and is fully confined to the source-ref ordering block; the author's ~15 is confirmed in kind and slightly understated in magnitude

concrete_defect_identified.defect: PyList_AsTuple returns a NEW reference; the previous list referenced by `sources` is overwritten without Py_DECREF, so the list (and its ob_item array) leaks once per decide() call that reaches the ordering block
concrete_defect_identified.why_this_is_the_site: the one-source path fails at cnt<2 BEFORE the ordering block and measures 0.0008 blocks/call, while the two-source path measures 17.0; the dedupe path (one surviving unique source) measures 12.0
concrete_defect_identified.correct_pattern_already_used_elsewhere: admit_relation lines 655-657 do it correctly: tup = PyList_AsTuple(srcs); Py_DECREF(srcs); srcs = tup;

other_memory_measurements.stage_b_resolve_exact_verdict: sub-linear residual that decays with N (0.13 -> 0.02 blocks/call) = interpreter lazy state, NOT a sustained leak; the author's 0.000 claim is not falsified as a leak

callback_and_construction_trust.observed: an owner constructed with entirely attacker-chosen relation class, snapshot class, semantic_hash, canonicalize and require_positive_authority seals successfully (sealed=True, counts=(1,1), 64-hex custody_hash) and exposes its pinned identities through the new read-only trusted_seam accessor
callback_and_construction_trust.improvement_since_the_frozen_stage_b: resolve_exact now refuses the inconsistent attacker stand-in with 'owner custody relation semantic hash mismatch' because the D8 projection re-hash is genuinely enforced
callback_and_construction_trust.what_is_ASSUMED: the three callables supplied at construction are the accepted pre553 implementations -- a harness responsibility
callback_and_construction_trust.what_is_DEMONSTRATED: once pinned, the identities cannot be re-bound from Python, and no live registry or Python owner is consulted for a positive
callback_and_construction_trust.what_is_NOT_provided: any provenance or authentication of the caller-chosen callables/classes. A production-owned sealed construction ingress is still required before adoption.
callback_and_construction_trust.verdict: acceptable ONLY as a TCB-assumed test seam inside the quarantined harness

ownership_of_post_loop_sorting.inspected: the source-ref ordering block copies each ref key and ref dict, sorts by key, dedupes adjacent equal keys and converts to a tuple
ownership_of_post_loop_sorting.ownership_defect: the final PyList_AsTuple reassignment loses the list reference (see concrete_defect_identified)
ownership_of_post_loop_sorting.no_corruption_observed: decision correctness, replay identity and the byte-exact custody hash are unaffected; the leak is bounded and per-call
